To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the barrier properties of a flake-filled composite can be predicted with high accuracy from knowledge of the two principal diffusions, normal and parallel, to the flake axes, (2) the barrier properties can be optimized by controlling the orientation of the flake axes and (3) the barrier properties are optimized when the flake axes are parallel to the macroscopic diffusion.
the barrier improvement factor (BIF) of flake-filled composite is maximized when the flake orientation is normal to the direction of diffusion.
the BIF of long-flake composites with a random flake orientation is maximized by aligning the flake axes with the direction of diffusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a model to predict the barrier properties of a flake-filled composite, with the aim to provide a guide to the design and manufacture of a microstructure with optimal barrier properties.
the development and validation of an analytical model for the prediction of the diffusion properties of flake filled composites.
the development and testing of a new theoretical model for the barrier properties of long, randomly oriented flakes, which is in agreement with both experimental and computational data.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed a new computational method to predict the barrier properties of long, flake-filled composite materials with precise control of flake orientation and have developed a new model which can accurately predict the diffusivity of these materials.
we have shown the importance of flake orientation on barrier properties, and that this effect can be accurately captured using a model that only requires two principal diffusivity values as inputs.
we have shown that the orientation of flakes can be used to control the diffusion properties of composites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the BIF is not a monotonic function of flake alignment and, in particular, that a significant barrier improvement can be achieved even at high values of misalignment.

the BIF can be maximized by orienting the flakes parallel to the direction of transport, but that a significant improvement is still possible at high misalignments, even when the flakes are randomly oriented.

, for the design of a flake-filled barrier, it is important to control the orientation of the flakes, and to ensure that this orientation is not too close to the direction of macroscopically diffusing solute.
